verdict_reason: The zigzag core is verified against the RELEASED reference twice, executed: (1) BLME's `_betti`/`span` reproduce `ZigZagLLMs/src/plots/post_process.POSTPROCESS` on the authors' own shipped 235,794-bar H1 barcode `llama_3_8b_dim_4_knn_4_last_token.csv` with max absolute difference EXACTLY 0 on the 33-entry beta_1 vector (14176, 15828, ..., 16321) and 0.0 on the 32-entry Z_1(l,l+1) row (0.0926, 0.2015, ..., 0.4335); (2) I ran the released `ZIGZAG.generate_simplex_tree` + `compute_layers_with_intersection` + `compute_filtration_times` + dionysus pipeline against BLME's `_true_zigzag_barcode` on 5 fixtures and got identical per-layer beta_1 ([1,1,1], [0,1,1], [1,1,1], [1,3,1,1], [2,3,4,4,6]), identical Z_adj and identical full-depth Z on 5/5, with kNN edge symmetric-difference 0 on 4/5 (1 edge on a degenerate collinear layer). The YELLOW is a residual: `_layer_topology`'s ABSOLUTE `np.maximum(dists, 1e-12)` edge floor is not scale-free. On a 40x4 Gaussian cloud all 200 kNN edges are strictly positive at every scale, yet at scale 1e-13, 1e-25 and 1e-30 ALL 200 are overwritten by the floor, turning the weighted geodesic into a hop metric and moving beta_1 from 3 to 6. Betti numbers are scale-invariant, so this is a genuine value-changing counterexample - but the shipped domain never reaches it (real gpt2 sentence-mean kNN distances are order 1-100), so it is a caveat, not a RED.
comparable_reason: Two exported scalars are EXACTLY n_layers on all three models I ran (gpt2/distilgpt2/pythia-70m, N=40, shipped k=5 / frac=0.1): h1_total_layer_persistence = 12.0 / 6.0 / 6.0 and h1_max_band_length = 12.0 / 6.0 / 6.0. Five more are constants: h1_num_bands = 1.0, betti1_fraction_layers = 1.0, h0_mean_components = 1.0, h0_persistence_range = 0.0, h1_first_layer = 0.0, h1_last_layer = 1.0, zz_true_full_depth = 0.0 - identical on all three. Only zz_true_adjacent_mean (0.4943 / 0.3892 / 0.1212) and zz_h1_turnover_rate (0.6526 / 0.7823 / 0.9265) carry model-distinguishing signal, and they are already the two the file tells callers to prefer. Nine of thirteen columns are either a depth restatement or a constant.

github_reason: Executed the released code twice as described in verdict_reason. Two facts I established by running rather than reading: (a) the standalone `sklearn.neighbors.kneighbors_graph(X, n_neighbors=k)` the release uses has `include_self=False`, so k means k REAL neighbours and BLME's k=5 aligns with the release's knn=5 - an earlier version of my own comparison used knn=k+1 and manufactured a 3x beta_1 mismatch that vanished on correct alignment, so the parameter alignment is the whole ballgame here; (b) on tie-heavy input the cKDTree substitution does diverge from sklearn: on an exact 5x5 lattice the edge symmetric-difference is 15 at k=4, 5 at k=5, 13 at k=6, while on 5/5 generic Gaussian/circle fixtures it is 0. Also verified that BLME's L-complex construction and the release's 2L-1 intersection construction give slightly different total bar counts (7 vs 6, 20 vs 19) from bars living only on an intersection index - which changes neither the layer beta_1 nor Z_p, the only quantities read.
paper_reason: Gardinazzi et al. (ICML 2025, arXiv:2410.11042) publish figures rather than a table of Z_p values that could be read to enough precision. The strongest available anchor is the authors' own shipped barcode artifact, and BLME reproduces the beta_1 vector and Z_1 row derived from it to exactly 0 error (above), which is a stronger check than a figure readout.
confounds_reason: h1_total_layer_persistence and h1_max_band_length equal n_layers exactly (12, 6, 6 for gpt2, distilgpt2, pythia-70m), a Pearson r of 1.0 with depth by construction: whenever betti1_fraction_layers saturates at 1.0 - which it does on all three models - the band summary can only report the number of layers. Those two columns ARE the depth. The identity-aware family (zz_true_adjacent_mean, zz_h1_turnover_rate) is not a depth restatement, but with 3 models I cannot separate it from d_model either; the file's own note that the raw cycle-rank counts scale with N (2.4 -> 65.5 as num_samples goes 40 -> 200) is why only the ratios are exported, and that is the right call.
defects: CODE / SCALE-DEPENDENT EDGE FLOOR, VALUE-CHANGING: zigzag.py:142 `vals = np.maximum(dists[:, 1:].ravel(), 1e-12)` is an ABSOLUTE floor applied to a scale-free construction. Measured on a 40x4 Gaussian cloud at k=5: at scale 1.0, 0/200 edges are overwritten and (beta_0, beta_1) = (1, 3); at scale 1e-13, 1e-25 and 1e-30, 200/200 strictly positive edges are overwritten and (beta_0, beta_1) = (1, 6). The floor exists only to stop scipy csgraph treating explicit zeros as absent edges, so it must be relative to the cloud, e.g. `max(d, 1e-12 * median_positive_distance)`. Note betti_curve.py has the same line but is IMMUNE, because its hop metric overwrites every weight with 1 and its beta_0 comes from `connected_components`, which ignores weights - so this is a zigzag-only exposure.

CODE / TIE POLICY vs THE RELEASE, tie-only: `_knn_edges` uses cKDTree where the release uses sklearn's ball_tree `kneighbors_graph`. Edge symmetric-difference on an exact 5x5 lattice: 15 (k=4), 5 (k=5), 13 (k=6). On 5/5 generic fixtures it is 0. Unreachable with float32 sentence means, which have no exact distance ties.

CODE / STALE COMMENT: zigzag.py:234-235 states 'No zigzag engine is installable here (dionysus needs boost and fails to build...)'. dionysus 2.1.1 imports and runs fine in this environment, and the `zz_true_*` family IS emitted end-to-end on real gpt2 reps (zz_true_n_bars = 58 at N=40). The comment contradicts the code 600 lines below it and will mislead the next reader into believing the GF(2) fallback is what ships.

CONFIG / DEGENERATE BAND FAMILY: at defaults.yaml num_samples=40, n_neighbors=5, persistence_frac=0.1 the H1 band summary saturates (betti1_fraction_layers = 1.0 on 3/3 models), which collapses h1_total_layer_persistence, h1_max_band_length, h1_num_bands, h1_first_layer and h1_last_layer to constants or to n_layers. The `_meta_h1_family_is_identically_zero` flag catches the opposite failure (all-zero) but not this one (all-one).
CODE / DOMAIN: the exact dionysus path is gated at n_pts >= 8 while `evaluate` accepts >= 3, so a small-corpus run silently loses all five zz_true_* keys with no `_meta_` flag saying so.

Delete or rewrite the stale 'no zigzag engine is installable' comment at zigzag.py:234-235; it is false in this environment and the dionysus path is the one that runs. Add a `_meta_h1_band_family_is_saturated` flag mirroring `_meta_h1_family_is_identically_zero`, and demote h1_total_layer_persistence / h1_max_band_length to `_meta_` - they equal n_layers whenever it fires.
